{{nihongo|'''Amatakekanakaya Shrine'''|天健金草神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Oki Province]].

[[ja:天健金草神社]]

'''Amatake Kanakaya Shrine''' (あまたけかなかやじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in Tsuma, {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|arz|اوكينوشيما|ceb|Okinoshima Chō|de|Okinoshima (Shimane)|es|Okinoshima (Shimane)|fa|اوکینوشیما، شیمانه|fr|Okinoshima|id|Okinoshima, Shimane|it|Okinoshima|ja|隠岐の島町|ko|오키노시마정|ms|Okinoshima, Shimane|my|အိုခိနိုရှိမမြို့၊ ရှိမနဲ|pl|Okinoshima|ru|Окиносима|sv|Okinoshima, Shimane|tl|Okinoshima, Shimane|tr|Okinoshima|ur|اوکینوشیما، شیمانے|zh|隱岐之島町|qid=Q1205039}}, {{ill|Oki District, Shimane|ar|منطقة أوكي (شيمانه)|ceb|Oki-gun|es|Distrito de Oki|fr|District d'Oki|hu|Oki körzet|id|Distrik Oki, Shimane|it|Distretto di Oki|ja|隠岐郡|ko|오키군|pl|Powiat Oki|pt|Distrito de Oki|simple|Oki District, Shimane|zh|隱岐郡|qid=Q735735}}, {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|Q132751|qid=Q132751}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} (minor shrine), and its former shrine rank was Prefectural Shrine.

=== History ===
It is said that the enshrined deities of this shrine displayed divine efficacy during {{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803}}’s {{ill|Three Han Campaign|Q11249435|qid=Q11249435}}, and that offerings were presented in the 2nd year of {{ill|Emperor Chūai|Q179971|qid=Q179971}} (193) {{sfn|Tsuma Village History Editorial Committee|1990|p=88}}.

According to the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}, in the 13th year of {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} (871), the shrine was granted the divine rank of Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade, in recognition of its contribution to prayers for national defense against {{ill|Silla|ar|مملكة شلا|ast|Silla (Corea)|az|Şila krallığı|azb|شیلا|bar|Silla|be|Сіла (дзяржава)|bg|Сила (държава)|bs|Kraljevstvo Sila|ca|Silla (Corea)|cdo|Sĭng-lò̤|ckb|شیللا|cs|Silla|da|Silla (koreansk stat)|de|Silla|eo|Silla|es|Silla (Corea)|eu|Silla (Korea)|fa|پادشاهی شیلا|fi|Silla|fr|Silla (Corée)|gl|Reino de Silla|hi|सिल्ला|hr|Kraljevstvo Sila|hu|Silla (ókori királyság)|id|Silla|it|Silla (Corea)|ja|新羅|ka|სილა|kk|Силла|km|ស៊ីលឡា|ko|신라|ks|سِللا سَلطَنَت|ku|Keyaniya Sillayê|lt|Šila (Korėja)|lv|Silla|mk|Сила (држава)|ml|സില്ല|mn|Шилла|ms|Silla|my|ရှီလာ|mzn|سیلا|nds|Silla|nl|Silla (Korea)|no|Silla|oc|Silla (reialme)|pl|Silla|pt|Silla (Coreia)|ro|Silla|ru|Силла|sco|Silla|sh|Sila (kraljevina)|si|සිල්ලා|simple|Silla|sk|Silla|sr|Сила (краљевство)|sv|Silla|sw|Silla|th|ชิลลา|tl|Silla|tr|Silla|uk|Сілла|vi|Tân La|wuu|新罗|zh|新罗|zh_classical|新羅|zh_min_nan|Sin-lô|zh_yue|新羅|qid=Q28456}} {{sfn|Tsuma Village History Editorial Committee|1990|p=86}}. According to the {{ill|Nihon Kiryaku|Q1053542|qid=Q1053542}}, in the 6th year of {{ill|Engi (era)|de|Engi (Ära)|fa|انگی (دوره)|fr|Ère Engi|ia|Engi (era)|id|Engi|ja|延喜|ko|엔기|ru|Энги (нэнго)|simple|Engi (era)|sr|Енги (ера)|tr|Engi (dönem)|uk|Енґі (ненґо)|zh|延喜|zh_yue|延喜|qid=Q1374325}} (906), Amatake Kanakaya-no-Mikoto caused “several Silla pirate ships” to retreat by means of a great wind {{sfn|Tsuma Village History Editorial Committee|1990|pp=86–87}}, and in the 3rd year of {{ill|Tengyō|Q1327340|qid=Q1327340}} (940) was granted Junior Third Rank {{sfn|Handa|1983|p=985}}. With the exception of {{ill|Kumano Taisha|ja|熊野大社|simple|Kumano Taisha|zh|熊野大社|qid=Q11568887}} and {{ill|Izumo-taisha|abstract|Q696362|ar|إزومو-تايشا|cs|Svatyně Izumo|de|Izumo-Taisha|es|Izumo Taisha|eu|Izumo-taisha|fi|Izumo-taisha|fr|Izumo-taisha|gl|Izumo Taisha|he|איזומו טאיישה|hu|Izumo-taisa|id|Izumo Taisha|it|Santuario di Izumo|ja|出雲大社|jv|Izumo Taisha|ka|იძუმო-ტაიშა|ko|이즈모 대사|la|Izumo-taisha|mk|Изумо-тајша|or|ଇଜୁମୋ ତାଇଶା|pl|Izumo-taisha|pt|Santuário de Izumo|ro|Marele Sanctuar de la Izumo|ru|Идзумо тайся|simple|Izumo-taisha|th|ศาลเจ้าอิซูโมะ|tr|Izumo-taisha|uk|Святилище Ідзумо|wuu|出云大社|zh|出雲大社|qid=Q696362}}, this divine rank was outstanding in the San’in region {{sfn|Handa|1983|p=985}}.

In the 3rd year of {{ill|Kankō|az|Kanko erası|de|Kankō|fa|کانکو|fr|Ère Kankō|ia|Kanko|id|Kankō|ja|寛弘|ko|간코|ru|Канко|simple|Kankō|sr|Канко|tr|Kankō|uk|Канко|zh|寬弘|zh_yue|寬弘|qid=Q2736722}} (1006), the shrine was relocated to its present site {{sfn|Tsuma Village History Editorial Committee|1990|p=1215}}.

In the medieval period, {{ill|Emperor Go-Daigo|azb|قودایقو (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Go-Daigo|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر گۆ-دایگۆ|cs|Go-Daigo|de|Go-Daigo|el|Αυτοκράτορας Γκο-Ντάιγκο|es|Go-Daigo Tennō|fa|امپراتور گودایگو|fi|Go-Daigo|fr|Go-Daigo|hak|Go-Daigo Thiên-fòng|hu|Go-Daigo japán császár|id|Kaisar Go-Daigo|it|Go-Daigo|ja|後醍醐天皇|jv|Kaisar Go-Daigo|ko|고다이고 천황|mr|गो-दाइगो|ms|Maharaja Go-Daigo|nl|Go-Daigo|pl|Go-Daigo|pt|Go-Daigo|ro|Împăratul Go-Daigo|ru|Император Го-Дайго|simple|Emperor Go-Daigo|sr|Го-Даиго|sv|Go-Daigo|sw|Go-Daigo wa Japani|th|จักรพรรดิโกไดโงะ|tl|Emperador Go-Daigo|tr|Go-Daigo|uk|Імператор Ґо-Дайґо|vi|Thiên hoàng Go-Daigo|wuu|后醍醐天皇|yo|Emperor Go-Daigo|zh|後醍醐天皇|zh_classical|後醍醐天皇|zh_min_nan|Go-Daigo Thian-hông|zh_yue|後醍醐天皇|qid=Q313942}}, who had been exiled to Oki, prayed at this shrine for his return to the capital, and when he succeeded in escaping from Oki, he granted it the rank of Senior First Rank {{sfn|Tsuma Village History Editorial Committee|1990|p=89}}{{efn|There is also an opinion that this Senior First Rank corresponds to a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Sōgen senji}}{{sfn|Handa|1983|p=985}}.}}. However, during this period, the Hachiman Shrine that was jointly enshrined became the primary focus of worship, and furthermore, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Takada Shrine}} came to attract the devotion of many people in this area {{sfn|Tsuma Village History Editorial Committee|1990|p=1164}}.

In the first year of {{ill|Bunkyū|ca|Era Bunkyū|de|Bunkyū|es|Bunkyū|fa|بونکیو (دوره)|fr|Ère Bunkyū|ia|Bunkyu|it|Bunkyū|ja|文久|ko|분큐|ru|Бункю|simple|Bunkyū|sr|Бункју|sv|Bunkyū|th|บุงกีว|tr|Bunkyū|zh|文久|qid=Q730266}} (1861), a fire destroyed not only the shrine buildings but also many treasures and ancient records {{sfn|Tsuma Village History Editorial Committee|1990|p=1216}}. In Meiji 5 (1872), the shrine was designated a {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=modern shrine ranking system}}, and later, in 1934 (Shōwa 9), it was elevated to Prefectural Shrine {{sfn|Tsuma Village History Editorial Committee|1990|p=1216}}.

=== Enshrined deities ===
=== Principal deities ===
* '''{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ōyatsuhime-no-Mikoto}}''' (おおやつひめのみこと)
* '''{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tsumatsuhime-no-Mikoto}}''' (つまつひめのみこと)
: These two deities are children of {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993}} and are said to have devoted themselves to land development, after which they resided respectively at “Ōya Sentō” and “Sayama Spring” {{sfn|Tsuma Village History Editorial Committee|1990|p=88}}. These two locations lie several kilometers from this shrine and were regarded as sacred sites where the deities descended, but eventually this shrine was founded at a place called “Hachimanbara,” where they came to be enshrined {{sfn|Tsuma Village History Editorial Committee|1990|p=88}}. There is a tradition that derives the place name “Tsuma” from Tsumatsuhime-no-Mikoto, but it is also said that the deity came to be enshrined based on an association with the place name {{sfn|Rika no Sha|1987|p=200}}.
* '''{{ill|Emperor Ōjin|qid=Q317997|lt=Hondawake-no-Mikoto|qid=Q317997}}''' (ほんだわけのみこと)
: One of the deities of the jointly enshrined Hachiman Shrine {{sfn|Handa|1983|p=984}}.

=== Subsidiary deities ===
* '''Okinagatara-shi-hime-no-Mikoto''' (おきながたらしひめのみこと)
: One of the deities of the jointly enshrined Hachiman Shrine {{sfn|Handa|1983|p=984}}.
* '''{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tamayori-hime-no-Mikoto}}''' (たまよりひめのみこと)
: One of the deities of the jointly enshrined Hachiman Shrine {{sfn|Handa|1983|p=984}}.
* '''{{ill|Shiotsuchi-no-Oji|Q11174872|qid=Q11174872|lt=Shiotsuchi no Oji}}''' (しおつちのおじ) {{sfn|Handa|1983|p=984}}
: One of the deities of the jointly enshrined Hachiman Shrine {{sfn|Handa|1983|p=984}}.
* '''{{ill|Takeminakata|qid=Q9150391|lt=Takeminakata-no-Mikoto|qid=Q9150391}}''' (たけみなかたのみこと)
: The deity of Suwa Shrine that was jointly enshrined in 1917 {{sfn|Handa|1983|p=984}}. Although this contradicts historical fact, there is a tradition that this Suwa Shrine was established in the first year of {{ill|Shōji (era)|fa|شوجی (دوره)|fr|Ère Shōji|ia|Shoji (era)|id|Shōji|ja|正治|ko|쇼지 (연호)|ru|Сёдзи (нэнго)|simple|Shōji (era)|sr|Шоџи (ера)|tr|Shōji (dönem)|zh|正治 (日本)|zh_yue|正治|qid=Q1199890}} (1199) by {{ill|Sasaki Yasukiyo|Q11382304|qid=Q11382304}} through a transfer from {{ill|Suwa-taisha|Q218813|qid=Q218813}} {{sfn|Tsuma Village History Editorial Committee|1990|p=116}}.

=== Facilities ===
[[File:Amatakekanakaya-Jinja Front.jpg|thumb|Shrine grounds of Amatake Kanakaya Shrine]]
[[File:Amatakekanakaya-Jinja Shrine.jpg|thumb|Main hall of Amatake Kanakaya Shrine]]
; Main hall
: A three-bay {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|Q210684|qid=Q210684}} structure with copper-sheet roofing {{sfn|Takahashi|1980|p=22}}{{efn|There is also a description stating iron-sheet roofing {{sfn|Handa|1983|p=986}}.}}, with a size of 7 tsubo {{sfn|Handa|1983|p=986}}. The framework was erected in the first year of {{ill|Genji era|Q1325419|qid=Q1325419}} (1864) {{sfn|Handa|1983|p=986}}. It has been noted that its floor plan resembles {{ill|Oki-zukuri|Q11659055|qid=Q11659055}} {{sfn|Takahashi|1980|p=23}}.
; Worship hall
: An {{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|Q855025|qid=Q855025}} structure with black tile roofing, measuring 11.5 tsubo {{sfn|Handa|1983|p=986}}. Built in 1917 (Taishō 6) {{sfn|Handa|1983|p=986}}.
; Offering hall
: An irimoya-zukuri structure with black tile roofing, measuring 6 tsubo {{sfn|Handa|1983|p=986}}.
; Zuijin Gate
: A {{ill|Kirizuma-style|Q13308575|qid=Q13308575}} structure with board roofing {{sfn|Handa|1983|p=986}}.
; Shrine office
: An irimoya-zukuri structure with black tile roofing {{sfn|Handa|1983|p=986}}.
; Auxiliary shrines
: Takeuchi Shrine (enshrined deity: {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|Q1073668|qid=Q1073668|lt=Takeuchi no Sukune-no-Mikoto}}) {{sfn|Tsuma Village History Editorial Committee|1990|p=1217}}
: Kasuga Shrine (enshrined deity: {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|fr|Ama-no-Koyane-no-mikoto|it|Ame-no-Koyane|ja|天児屋命|mni|ꯑꯃꯦ-ꯅꯣ-ꯀꯣꯌꯅꯦ|pt|Ame-no-Koyane|ru|Амэ-но коянэ-но микото|simple|Ame-no-Koyane|zh|天兒屋命|qid=Q2564508|lt=Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto}}) {{sfn|Tsuma Village History Editorial Committee|1990|p=1217}}
: Manito Shrine (enshrined deities: fifteen goddesses) {{sfn|Tsuma Village History Editorial Committee|1990|p=1217}}
; Other
: One Myōjin torii made of {{ill|Castanopsis|Q1065400|qid=Q1065400|lt=chinquapin}} wood {{sfn|Handa|1983|p=986}}. One pair each of stone lanterns and karajishi lion-dogs {{sfn|Handa|1983|p=986}}.
: The former shrine site is located at Hachimanbara, Tsuma, Okinoshima Town, and foundation stones remain {{sfn|Handa|1983|p=986}}.
